Preprint — arXiv:2607.21217v1 [cs.AI]; no published venue stated
Fudan University (Peng, Xu, Xiao, Hong, Y. Cao); Meituan Group, industry (Peng, Zhang, Qiu, X. Cao, He); Singapore Management University (Huang, Lo); Shanghai Innovation Institute (Xu, Y. Cao)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — ICAE-Bench, a benchmark of 480 interactive from-scratch repository-generation tasks (plus 50-task ICAE-Bench-Lite) where the coding agent starts from a fuzzy PRD and may query a grounded User Agent; six models compared under Claude Code, and Claude Code vs OpenHands on Lite, with ablations

No SDD approach. Configurations compared: agent frameworks Claude Code (via claude-agent-sdk-python, version not stated) and OpenHands (version not stated) with models GPT-5.5, Claude-Opus-4.8, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, GLM-5.1, Gemini-3.1-Pro, MiniMax-M2.5; requirement-exposure conditions Fuzzy L1 (default), L2, L3, RecoveredPRD and GroundPRD (complete PRD, upper-bound reference)

Benchmark artefacts, not a development method: GroundPRD (detailed natural-language product requirement document with embedded example cases), fuzzy PRD (L1 150-250-word PM-style request; L2; L3), User Agent Data (hidden constraints with trigger keywords and grounded responses, context pointers, golden API signature, fallback response), Public/Native/Enhanced black-box JSON cases, ultimate Docker image. The agent must deliver a runnable repository with rcb_tests/test.sh entry point and self-check cases

Benchmark construction (offline): repository filtering, GroundPRD synthesis and test refactoring, PRD fuzzification, ultimate-image packaging, artifact verification. Run (online): agent reads fuzzy PRD, asks clarification questions to the User Agent within a budget (default 16), develops/runs/debugs in the container, self-checks against recovered Public cases; then multi-dimensional evaluation in a fresh container

None in the agent workflow (User Agent is an LLM router simulating the stakeholder; no human in the loop). Humans only in benchmark construction checks (inspection of failing cases during GroundPRD reconstruction) and in validating critic scores on 200 repositories
N/A (no SDD approach); full agent workflows run on the benchmark, from fuzzy or complete PRD to repository
Not classifiable (benchmark of coding agents; a PRD is the input, no SDD terms used by the authors)
New project (0-to-1 repository generation from a PRD in a provisioned container; golden code removed)

480 tasks from real open-source repositories, 40 per language; golden LOC 318 to 2,918,810 (mean 35,533), golden files 4 to 17,488 (mean 258). ICAE-Bench-Lite: 50 smallest tasks, 10 languages, golden LOC 318-1,509 (mean 979), files 4-61 (mean 17). GroundPRD mean 6,764 tokens (full) / 6,170 (Lite)

Mixed open-source software (categories: developer and build tools, web and HTTP services, utility libraries, DevOps and cloud, database and storage, UI/frontend/mobile, authentication and security, data serialization and parsing, testing and QA, ML and data science); 12 languages: C#, C++, Dart, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, TypeScript
N/A (no human participants; simulated user). Three graduate annotators for critic validation

Mean generation time (s) per repository and tokens per repository (input, output, cache-creation and cache-read summed from settings.json) for the main Claude Code runs, figure only (Fig. 11); interaction budget usage (issued queries / budget)

Case-level pass rate on black-box cases: Overall = (passed Native + passed Enhanced)/(Native + Enhanced); Public, Native, Enhanced views; failure modes per suite (Mismatch, Missing, Exec., No Test); Clean repositories (all cases pass)

Design quality (critic LLM static review, 0-1, architecture and separation of core logic from adapter); structural assessment: file-count and LOC ratios to golden, class, method and namespace/package similarity
None
Semantic similarity and API similarity (critic LLM, 0-1); interaction quality: constraint coverage |H|/|C|, fallback rate, budget usage (macro-averaged per task)

Automatic: generated repository replayed in a fresh container from the same image, authoritative cases injected, outputs compared on the host; router logs for interaction metrics; critic model static review of generated vs golden trees (critic model not named) for semantic/API/design scores; tokens and time from exported per-run settings.json. Manual: three graduate annotators scored 200 sampled repositories to validate critic scores (Pearson 0.372-0.471, ICC(A,1) 0.221-0.269)

No success criterion stated by the authors for any configuration (quality and cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors). Cost: tokens and time per repository in Fig. 11 only

Tasks: 480 (full) and 50 (Lite) repository-generation tasks. Configurations: 6 models under Claude Code (full and Lite); 6 models under OpenHands (Lite); requirement-exposure levels; single-factor ablations on Lite. Baseline/reference: GroundPRD as upper bound; Fuzzy L1 + User Agent as default. Held constant: tasks, fuzzy PRD, User Agent (DeepSeek-V3.2, same prompt and records), query budget 16, task instruction prompt, container image, evaluation harness; thinking adaptive unless stated. Acceptance tests: authoritative black-box Native and Enhanced cases run in a fresh container. Repetitions: not stated (one run per configuration reported; no variance). Human intervention: none (automated harness)

Full split: Claude-Opus-4.8 best Overall (38.2%), GPT-5.5 37.2%, MiniMax-M2.5 0.8%; on Lite GPT-5.5 first (53.3%) and Opus second (Spearman rho 0.71 between splits). GroundPRD best for four of six models; RecoveredPRD below GroundPRD for four models; interaction recovers only part of the gap. OpenHands lower than Claude Code for every model (GPT-5.5 -21.8 points, Opus -5.5), changing the ranking. Executable Public case files +24.4 points; thinking enabled +9.9 (Gemini); larger budget, stronger User Agent coverage and richer image non-monotonic or lower. Higher constraint coverage does not mean higher pass rate. No significance tests

Distinguished models (0.8% to 38.2% Overall) and frameworks; authors state Lite preserves the top tier but not definitive model ranking or language-level conclusions (rho 0.71); critic metrics agree only moderately with humans (Pearson 0.37-0.47) and are complementary to tests; runtime and tokens are weak proxies for correctness. Repeatability not assessed (no repeated runs)

Lite not suitable for definitive ranking or language-level conclusions; moderate agreement of critic scores with human ratings; fuzzy levels are an operational hierarchy, not a universal scale; constraint forgetting and interaction inefficiency not directly identifiable from execution outcomes. Gap: agents fail to preserve clarified requirements and turn them into coherent implementations (information-to-execution gap). Future work: end-to-end multimodal scenarios, frontend tasks, integration with OpenClaw

Benchmark, dataset and evaluation code: https://github.com/ALEX-nlp/ICAE-EVAL. Prompts in Appendices A-I. Values from Tables VI, VII, IX-XV (text extraction of tables partly jumbled; rows rebuilt and checked against text claims; Table V token statistics also rebuilt). Reporting inconsistencies: text says OpenHands lowers Overall 'for every model by 5.5-21.8 points' (p. 10-11) but Table X gives MiniMax-M2.5 2.8 -> 1.1 (-1.7); Table X Claude Code GLM-5.1 value 37.4 is the think-8k setting while Table VII reports 40.0 (adaptive), so the GLM row of the framework comparison uses think-8k although the main tables use adaptive thinking; the paper says the coding agent works in the ultimate image (p. 2, 5), but Table XIV gives GLM-5.1 think-8k 37.4 with the base image and 28.4 with the ultimate image, and 37.4 is the value reported as the default in Tables IX, X, XI and XIII, so the default runs appear to use the base image. Construction relies on LLMs (Claude-Opus-4.8 reconstruction, GPT-5.5 judge). No pre-registration. Programming languages: 12 (C#, C++, Dart, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, TypeScript)
